title: Atrial flutter with 4:1 conduction
summary: Same circuit as typical flutter, but the AV node passes only every fourth wave.

events.label: Circuit
events.caption: The same macro-reentrant circuit around the tricuspid annulus produces flutter waves 300 times a minute.

events.label: Conducted beat
events.caption: A conducted impulse activates the ventricles through the normal system.
events.ecg: A narrow QRS superimposed on the flutter waves.

events.label: Blocked waves
events.caption: With a longer AV node refractory period, the next three flutter waves reach the node too early and are blocked.
events.ecg: Four flutter waves for each QRS.

events.label: Next conducted beat
events.caption: The fourth wave after the last conducted one gets through. Ventricular rate about 75 per minute.
events.ecg: A slow, regular ventricular rhythm: 4:1 conduction.

teaching_points: The ventricular response in flutter depends on the AV node: 2:1 is common, 4:1 and variable block also occur.
Flutter should be suspected whenever a regular narrow-complex rhythm runs at a ventricular rate near 150 or 75.
Slowing AV conduction does not stop the flutter; it only changes the ventricular response.
